chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukatab who was killed and said: “The portion of him that had become free is calculated, so the diyah of a free man is paid for it, and for the portion that remained in bondage, the diyah of a slave is paid.”
And he said: “A slave does not impose upon his family any liability beyond himself.”

key_terms.دِيَةُ الْحُرِّ: The blood money due for the life of a free person.
key_terms.دِيَةُ الْعَبْدِ: The blood money due for the life of a slave.
key_terms.لَا يُغْرِمُ أَهْلَهُ: Does not cause his family to bear financial liability.
key_terms.مَا رَقَّ: The portion that remained in bondage or slavery.
key_terms.مَا عَتَقَ مِنْهُ: The portion of the mukatab that had attained freedom.
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: A slave under a contractual arrangement to earn or purchase freedom.

ai.seo_question: How is the diyah of a mukatab calculated in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the diyah of a mukatab who is killed, distinguishing between the portion of his status that had attained freedom and the portion that remained in bondage. It also establishes that a slave’s liability does not extend beyond his own person to burden his family.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5264 - Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as), Commander of the Faithful, ruled regarding a mukatab (a slave who had a contract for freedom) who was killed: "The portion of him that had been freed is calculated, and the blood money for that part is paid as that of a free man, and the portion that remained in servitude is paid as the blood money of a slave."
Imam (as) also said: "A slave does not burden his family with any liability beyond himself."
